title: Initial Snapshot Characterization
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with a binary state code, let $m\in\mathbb N$, let $a:\mathbb N\to\{0,1\}$, and let $y$ be a Boolean word of length $m$. Suppose $a(j)$ agrees with the bit of $y$ at zero-based position $j$ for every $j<m$. Then the initial-template condition for the assignment at time zero holds if and only if the raw block at time zero equals the encoding of $M$'s initial snapshot on $y$.
hypotheses_covered: A binary code for optional states of $M$
For every $j<m$, $a(j)$ equals the $j$-th bit of $y$, defaulting to false if absent
replaced: Let $y$ be a word of length $m$ and let the assignment agree with $y$ on the first $m$ variables. Then the initial meaning holds exactly when the raw block at time zero equals the encoding of the machine's genuine initial snapshot on $y$, with the empty-input case included.
